note: The rounds this project owes, as data. A date in a roadmap table is a date nobody can assert on; this file is read by eval/tools/round_clock.py on every push, so a registered round that passes its date turns CI red instead of being discovered the next time somebody reads the plan. `status` moves registered -> dispatched -> read, or to `cancelled`, which is a decision rather than a debt. Nothing here fires on a clock: two dispatches in this lane were armed on a `schedule:` trigger and neither fired (AUDIT 34.232, 34.241), so a funded action is a `workflow_dispatch` and the cron is left to the free contract job.

rounds.title: the placement's price — front against tail, one dispatch
the reliability column — four attempts, control against front
rounds.outcome: refuted on two of five bars

rounds.title: the placebo, interleaved — two identical arms, task by task, registered delta of zero
rounds.why: R218b found the same treatment arm reading 86.84, 81.60 and 78.07 in one afternoon, and the arms in its grid ran 35 minutes apart. Two identical arms interleaved task by task must read zero; if they do not, no contrast on this grid is measurable and the repair is the grid.
rounds.outcome: the grid is usable and the asymmetry bar was mis-specified: 4 of 5 endpoints hold, the fifth by one task

reading.verdict: ORDER_ASYMMETRIC: 16 against 13 is three tasks past a two-task window on 29 discordant pairs, which is p = 0.71
reading.finding: turnover does not shrink when the gap shrinks 30x: 25.4% at 71 s against R218b's 22% at 35 min, so the drift is sampling noise rather than a time confound, and no schedule repairs it

rounds.title: the dose inside the task — does an attempt that received more material pass more often
rounds.outcome: built and read on R218b's documents: NO_DOSE on both arms, because a front-placement block never enters the transcript
rounds.why: Every flat reading this lane has is a between-arm mean. Within one task, the four attempts of R218b received different amounts of material, and comparing them holds the difficulty fixed — the one decomposition a two-arm grid cannot make.

reading.control: 456 episodes, 0 with a block, state NO_DOSE
reading.front: 456 episodes, 0 with a block, state NO_DOSE — while the log counts 4,341 renders
reading.whyNoDose: the block goes into `state.system_messages`, which is composed into the request; `grep -c microglia-board` over 32 MB of front.json is 0

reconstructionTried.verdict: not implemented — the ordering is turn count, which is the same variable that makes a retail episode fail

reading.repair: R218e records the dose at the source, per episode

rounds.title: the dose, recorded where it is known — one line an episode, written by the arm
rounds.why: R218d could not read a treated arm's material because the material was never written down: the block is in the request and the transcript is the conversation. One JSONL line an episode — turns, block characters, renders, the final verdict — turns the question the lane keeps asking into one it can answer per episode. The recording is the only route: the transcript holds no prompt.
rounds.amended: Registered 25 November with 114 episodes and a transcript check. Amended 26 November, before dispatch, on three measurements that cost nothing: (1) tau2 stores no `system` message at either placement, so the transcript check is impossible and is replaced by an identity against the phase census; (2) one attempt a task cannot produce a within-task pair, so the grid is 114 x 2 rounds; (3) the trial index is the round, not a turn count.
rounds.build: agent records one dict an episode (turns/renders/chars/written/changes/stable) at the single boundary site; runner resolves text->task and partitions by round; eval/drivers/tau2/dose.py joins and refuses three states; board_dose.py --sidecar reads it, and answers NO_SYSTEM on a transcript
rounds.outcome: DOSE_READ, and the dose is null at both scales: over the 114 tasks whose two rounds received different amounts the higher-dose side read above on 14 and below on 14 with 86 level (p = 1.0000), and on the 17 tasks whose sides averaged within one turn of each other it read 2 against 3 with 12 level (p = 1.0000). The recorded block averages 1,421 characters an episode and 222 of 228 episodes carried one, so the material was present and its size varied by a median of 820 characters — and more of it changed nothing.

reading.verdict: the full grid is a sign test with power and no direction (28 discordant tasks, 14-14, p = 1.0); the length-matched subset is a direction with no power (5 discordant tasks, 2-3, p = 1.0, and five is under the six a unanimous test needs). Neither supports the premise, and the pre-registered rule returns a bound rather than a verdict because the decided subset is one task short of six.
reading.unit: the sign test reads tasks and not attempts. An attempt inside a task is not an independent draw, and the first read of this grid counted passing attempts instead — 180 of them standing in for 114 pairs, reported as '90 against 90 attempt-pairs' (AUDIT 34.313). The correction changed no verdict and changed every number in the sentence.

rounds.title: the invocation policy — serve the state when a write needs it, not when it is renderable
rounds.amended: Registered 2026-11-25 with arms front+policy. Amended 2026-11-26, before dispatch: the tail is the placement the product ships (R216b, serving-defaults.json), so the rule is tested at the tail; testing it at the front would price a treatment the product does not use.
rounds.why: The block has two state lines and two judgment lines. The judgments are the parser's claims about the request, and `goal_board.py --accusations` reads 1,808 of 1,965 of them (92.0%) on R218b's front arm as naming a family the task requires a write in. The rule admits state and refuses to admit judgment; the bar is a count in one stratum (regressions 6 -> <=1, rescues >=12 of 15).
rounds.outcome: read, then not replicated. The first dispatch read +10.5 pp; the identical second read -0.9 pp. Pooled +4.8 pp [-1.2, +10.8], McNemar p = 0.152: no accuracy claim. The mechanism replicated exactly in both (admission all/state, chars -8%, changes -19%, bill -4% and -7%), so the null is about the effect and not about the treatment.

reading.caveat: the strata use R218b's control arm because this dispatch ran no control; the paired board-vs-policy contrast is within one dispatch and is the claim

rounds.title: one manifest, two readers — the configuration the eval measured is the one the product ships
rounds.outcome: built; the probe now prices the shipped placement and --board names the population

rounds.title: the same two arms, again — a replication before the rule becomes a default
rounds.why: R219 read +10.5 pp [+0.4, +20.5] with p = 0.029 on 19 moved and 7 broke. The grid's identical arms turn over 25.4% of their tasks, so 26 discordant pairs is what noise produces and only the asymmetry is the signal. A replication is the cheapest instrument for a single dispatch, and the product default does not move until the sign repeats.
rounds.outcome: NO_LIFT: the first reading did not replicate

rounds.title: the admission rule at a resolution that could see it — 800 tasks, or not at all
rounds.why: Pooled over two dispatches the rule is +4.8 pp [-1.2, +10.8]: inside the 13.2 pp a 114-task grid can resolve (R218c), which is why the first dispatch's +10.5 pp did not replicate. An accuracy claim would need ~800 tasks a contrast, 1,600 episodes, about $7.4 = CNY 53. Registered so the option is priced rather than forgotten; it is NOT the next item, because the rule is a correctness repair and the cost saving is already measured at -4% and -7%.
rounds.outcome: cancelled on its own arithmetic: the registration prices 1,600 episodes at $7.4 to resolve the rule's +4.8 pp, but the decomposition fitted from R218b says 4.8 pp needs 10.95 attempts a task and 2,497 episodes, $13.73 — the label was 85% low because it assumed episodes are independent when the task-level spread says otherwise. At $7.4 the round would have bought about 70% power, which is the worst purchase available: enough to run, not enough to believe.

rounds.title: the price of a move, measured rather than derived — what R216b's -4% is made of
rounds.why: R216b read the shipped tail at -4% against the second-system shape and explained it with a number it never measured: a change behind the conversation re-bills the block, a change in front of it re-bills everything behind it. `movePrice` computes that from the provider's own cache counters and the probe has always been able to ask for it with --rewrite-at; no dispatch ever has. A derived explanation of a measured bill is the shape this project refuses.
rounds.instrument: pnpm eval:cache-probe --rewrite-at 10 (five shapes, nine turns, one changed call each: cents)
rounds.outcome: read and REFUTED: a move costs the same 2,010 tokens wherever the block sits, so the tail is not the cheap placement the derivation assumed

reading.prediction: tail < system-second < system-merged < first-turn, with the tail within one block of zero
reading.verdict: the ordering is refuted: the three conversation-adjacent shapes price identically at 2,010.5 tokens, 1.34 blocks, and the first-turn shape is the cheapest at 1,882.5 — the tail is not cheaper than a front placement, and R216b's -4% therefore keeps no derivation
reading.steadyState: a second system message is re-billed 17 tokens a call over the control, inside the 128-token tolerance, so the steady-state premium is not where the -4% lives either

rounds.title: when nothing should be served — the serving decision screened before it is armed
rounds.outcome: screened, not armed: 385 prefix cuts over R218b's 228 pairs yielded one admissible policy, and it did not replicate on the held-out half
rounds.why: The stratified reading says the block is worth +7.5 points on the half-solved tasks and costs -9.5 on the solved ones, so the decision worth money is whether to serve at all. That decision needs an observable that exists before the outcome, and a replay over the one grid holding both arms prices any candidate for nothing.

reading.screen: 35% skipped, skipDelta +13.8 pp on 15 discordant pairs (13 up, 2 down), p = 0.0074
reading.confirm: 59% served, skipDelta +3.2 pp on 21 discordant pairs (12 up, 9 down), p = 0.66 — NOT_CONFIRMED
reading.pooled: skipDelta +8.1 pp on 36 discordant pairs (25 up, 11 down), p = 0.029, DOMINATED on the serve half

refutedForFree.askCount: 110 of 114 openings state at least one ask, so a gate serves 96.5%
refutedForFree.firstToolFamily: the first call is an identity lookup in 452 of 456 episodes, so a gate serves 99.1%

reading.taskLevel: the opening turn is constant across a task's four attempts on 100% of tasks, so the only admissible cut was an admission rule and not a serving gate

resolution.domain: retail, 114 tasks — the whole domain, so the task count is a ceiling and not a choice
resolution.wallMeans: repeating a task lowers only the measurement half of the error; at 114 tasks the other half is the floor, so no budget resolves an effect below 3.21 pp inside this domain
resolution.whyItMatters: the 0.23 pp between this project and the strongest text row, and the 3.2 pp of this project's own largest measured effect, both sit under the floor — so a point-estimate claim on this domain is unprovable in either direction, and more episodes cannot change that

rounds.title: reconstruct the memory against the live state — priced before it was registered, and refused
rounds.why: The literature's strongest published gate is a content repair rather than a serving one: reconstruct the memory against the current state and ALFWorld reads 85.2 against 79.6 without. This project's own stratification measures the same harm, so the round would test whether reconstruction recovers it.
rounds.outcome: cancelled for nothing, before dispatch: a content repair can only reach the tasks whose material was wrong, and this project's harm is not in the tasks whose material was wrong. The 66 tasks a no-memory arm solved every attempt lose 9.5 pp by being served at all, which a better sentence does not fix. Crediting the whole published 5.6 pp to the mixed stratum gives +2.11 pp at the arm level; doubling that gain gives +2.83 pp. Both are under the domain's 3.21 pp floor, so the round could not have produced a readable result at any sample size this budget allows.

rounds.title: what the episode reveals — the serving decision read from the payload rather than from the request
rounds.why: R223 closed the space of things a request declares and named its successor in the same document: read what the episode reveals. The lane had never read the first state payload, and R223 pre-committed the consequence of that reading being empty — that the harm is a property of the material's presence and not of its content. A screen over a grid already on disk decides it for nothing.
rounds.outcome: screened and REFUTED: 565 reveal-keyed cuts over R218b's 456 pairs yield 18 admissible, against 14.1 from noise alone (z = +1.04, p = 0.148), and the cut the screen chose reverses sign on the half it never saw

reading.confirm: skips 66% of the pairs for -6.5 pp on 17 discordant pairs (6 up, 11 down), p = 0.3323, and serves the rest at -2.0 pp — NOT_CONFIRMED
reading.pooled: +1.8 pp against serving everything and +0.2 pp against serving nothing, DOMINATED on the serve half
reading.taskConstancy: the reveal is nearly as task-constant as the request: revealEntries and revealChars vary inside a task on 11% of tasks, against 4% for the first tool call, so a cut on it is an admission rule for a task class and not a gate for one attempt
reading.boundary: the prefix now ends at the reveal's own result, which is the turn R219's invocation policy serves on, so the gate is implementable rather than counterfactual
reading.consequence: no observable decision recovers the +7.5 / -9.5 stratification, from the request (R223) or from the reveal (R225), so the harm belongs to the material's presence

rounds.title: the airline grid, admitted or refused before it is bought — the two numbers applied to the last purchase
rounds.why: R223's test cancelled two rounds. The queue still holds one purchase, and no document had applied the test to it: 50 independent tasks in a domain this project has never measured. The floor for that grid and the mechanism's largest measured effect decide it, and both are arithmetic on artefacts already on disk.
rounds.outcome: ADMITTED at the four-attempt rung by 1.18 pp: a 50-task grid resolves 6.72 pp at four attempts against a mechanism measured at 7.90, and 12.24 pp at one attempt, which fails outright

reading.priceCorrected: 400 episodes at the measured $0.0052-0.0056 is $2.20, about CNY 16, against the CNY 5.4 the queue carried: the queue's figure was registered when the round was one attempt an arm, and the design it needs is four
reading.assumption: the floor transfers retail's b = 0.01496 to airline; b is a property of the domain and airline's is unknown until an airline grid exists, so the transfer buys an order of magnitude and not a number
reading.whyAirlineAtAll: not resolution — airline is worse per task than retail at 50 tasks against 114 — but a second domain, which is the only thing that can say whether a finding is about memory or about retail

rounds.title: the airline parser — the board's families and receipts, taught the domain before it is dispatched into
rounds.why: R226 admits R217 and names what blocks it: FAMILIES maps retail write tools to ask families, and an airline transcript's writes are not in it, so a dispatch today would serve a block whose items never settle. That is not a null result, it is a broken instrument reporting one, and the census that prevents it costs nothing because the airline tasks carry their own required actions.
rounds.bar: the parser's family recall on the 50 airline requests at or above the retail parser's own, measured by --census before any dispatch is armed
rounds.outcome: REFUTED: the retail parser reaches 15 of 50 required airline writes (30.0% family recall) against its own 83.3% on retail, measured by the same census, so R217 is cancelled before dispatch

reading.instrument: eval/tools/goal_board.py --census over eval/manifests/airline-goals.json, built from tau2 v1.0.1's own airline tasks.json: 50 tasks, 50 required writes, 7 with none
reading.whatWasBuilt: five airline write tools enter FAMILIES (cancel_reservation, update_reservation_flights, the passenger and baggage updates, book_reservation) and three cues enter the shared table after the retail seven, which the unchanged retail census is what proves harmless

decomposition.askIsNotTheAction: 5 cancel misses and the 1 transfer are cases where the policy makes the correct action a different family from the stated ask: a change is settled by cancel-and-rebook, and a refusal is settled by a transfer
decomposition.noActionVerb: 5 book misses include requests that state only a route ("you want to fly from New York to Seattle") and asks phrased as "make a reservation", which names an object and no action
decomposition.cuePriority: modify fires before passenger and baggage, so "change the passenger to yourself" reports a modify; one clause carries one family and these asks carry two
decomposition.domainCollision: the retail cue for `return` fires on "the return flight is May 20" in 5 tasks, where return names a leg and not a request

reading.whyItIsNotAVocabularyProblem: two of the four causes are properties of the domain rather than gaps in a word list, and the board's contract is what they break: an ask settles against a receipt of the same family, which holds in a catalogue domain where the request names the action and does not hold where the action is a policy consequence

rounds.title: the airline column — 50 independent tasks, a second domain, and the transfer of the mechanism
rounds.why: Retail's floor is 3.21 pp and no budget lowers it, so the only purchase that buys anything is more independent tasks in a domain not yet measured. Airline is 50 tasks, its published column is unsaturated (top 84.0, median 63.8 over 24 rows), and R226 prices the grid at 6.72 pp of resolution at four attempts against a mechanism measured at 7.90.
rounds.bar: the paired pass^1 delta at the four-attempt rung, with the served share and the two conditional columns beside it; a reading inside 6.72 pp is a statement about the grid and is reported as one
rounds.priceNote: CNY 16 at the measured rate, not the CNY 5.4 the queue carried (R226, AUDIT 34.316)
rounds.outcome: cancelled by its own prerequisite: R217a measured the transfer at 30.0% family recall against retail's 83.3%, and a block whose items never settle is a broken instrument rather than a null result

rounds.title: settle by the record, not by the family — the contract the airline domain actually supports
rounds.why: R217a's refutation is not a vocabulary gap: two of its four causes are that the correct action has a different family from the stated ask (a change is settled by cancel-and-rebook) and that "return" names a leg in this domain. The board settles an ask against a receipt of the same family, which is a contract a catalogue domain supports and a policy domain does not. The successor rewrites the contract rather than the word list: an ask settles against a receipt that touches the record it names, whatever family that receipt is in.
rounds.bar: family recall is replaced by a record-recall bar: on the 50 airline requests, the share of required writes whose record the parser names, at or above 0.75, measured by the same census before any dispatch
rounds.outcome: REFUTED: 27 of 50 graded airline writes are named by their record (54.0%) against the registered 0.75 bar, and 30 of 50 with the family rule the round retires; the misses are 13 writes on asks that select a set of records by a predicate and 6 bookings whose object the policy chooses, so the reference in this corpus is a set or a decision rather than a record

rounds.title: bind the item to the read, not to the words — the settlement a policy domain can support
rounds.why: R227 closed the record rule at 54.0% and named why: 13 of its 23 misses are asks over a *set* of records selected by a predicate the request never spells as tokens ("all your upcoming flights", "flights longer than four hours", "multiple flights for the same day"), and 6 are bookings whose object the policy chooses. A reference that neither the words nor the record can supply is supplied by the agent's own reads, which this lane has never used as the anchor. The successor binds each item to the record the episode reads and settles it on the write that touches that record, and it is measurable at zero cost on the retail grid the lane already owns.
rounds.bar: on the retail grid already on disk, the read-anchored board must settle at least as many of its writing episodes as the request-anchored board does (the 1.18 pp admission R226 priced), while its false-accusation rate does not rise
rounds.outcome: REFUTED on B3: the read-anchored board settles 644 of 654 discharged required writes (98.5%) against the request board's 416 (63.6%) and credits zero calls to nothing, but it opens 1019 items no required write needs (2.53 per episode against 1.79 required), and the open-tax bar refuses it on both grids (2.53/1.79 and 2.54/1.81)

rounds.title: an item is an ask, and the read supplies the binding
rounds.why: R228 priced two rules against each other and neither is a working memory: the request board attributes 63.6% of the required writes and accuses 232 calls, the read board attributes 98.5% and opens 2.53 unneeded items per episode. The two failures are one representational fact — what is required is only in the request, and which record a call touched is only in the read — so the successor binds an ask to a write of its family that touches a record the episode opened.
rounds.bar: coverage of discharged required writes at or above the request board's on the same episodes, unaccounted writes at or below its 232, and at least 0.90 of the board's ticks backed by a graded write
rounds.outcome: REFUTED on B1: the conjunction keeps the request board's items and gains 10 complete episodes while losing 12, covering 415 of 654 writes (63.5%) against the request board's 416, so the read rule's completeness came from having no ask at all; it holds on the replication (+1.7pp, 404 against 393), which is reported as a property of the grids, not as a pass. Its taxonomy is the round's real result: 155 of the 232 misses are asks stated after the first user turn, 61 are asks already spent, 16 are never stated

rounds.title: admit a later-turn ask only from a turn that is not an answer
rounds.why: R229's taxonomy put 155 of its 232 unattributed writes on asks the conversation states after the first user turn, which makes disclosure order the largest defect this lane has measured in the block's own content. Following the conversation is not the repair either: the same binding rule over every user turn reaches 95.6% of the required writes at 4761 items, 4.9x the turn-one contract, because a user's *answer* can contain a cue word and be read as an ask. The successor tests the one discriminator that needs no vocabulary: an ask is admitted from a later turn only when the agent's previous turn did not ask the user a question, so a reply to a question is not a requirement.
rounds.bar: of the 155 writes R229 attributed to later-turn asks, at least 60% must still be accounted for; the admitted asks must not exceed twice the turn-one contract's 970 items; and coverage must rise at least 10 points over the request board's 63.6%
rounds.outcome: REFUTED on B1 and B3: 25 of the 155 later-turn writes are recovered (16.1% against a bar of 60%) and the admitted board covers 410 of 654 required writes (62.7%, below the request board's 416); only the noise bar holds, at 1,110 items against 1,940. The mechanism is a property of the corpus's user model rather than of the rule: 1,893 of 2,453 user turns (77.2%) follow an assistant question, so the discriminator admits 560 turns and refuses 1,893 - the requirement and the answer share a turn. A second, independent loss is visible in the same reading: 52 episodes read their contract from a turn that is not turn one, because the first turn stated no ask and `request_of` falls back, and the filter refused exactly that turn in 50 of them, which is how a board that reads more turns covers fewer writes. The replication repeats all three: 20 of 156 (12.8%), 63.9% against 61.1%, 1,043 items, 1,876 of 2,422 turns preceded by a question.

rounds.title: admit the requirement clause, not the turn
rounds.why: R230 established that the requirement and the answer share a turn: 77.2% of user turns follow an assistant question, so a turn-level filter discards 84% of the requirements disclosed after turn one and lands below the contract it was meant to extend. The material is therefore inside the turn, and the next discriminator has to be the clause - the one that carries a requirement verb and an object - with turn position demoted from gate to tie-break.
rounds.bar: registered in prereg/R231-the-clause.md before the reading; not yet read
rounds.outcome: REFUTED on B2 alone: 154 of the 155 later-turn writes are recovered (99.4% against a bar of 60%) and coverage reaches 95.4% against a bar of 73.6%, but the board pays 2,729 items over the contract for those 154 writes - 17.72 each against a budget of 1.5. The two bars that hold are the round's real result: restricting inheritance to the contract's turn reaches askAll's coverage (624 against 625 of 654) while dropping 1,153 of the 5,311 asks the parser offers, so inheritance is 22% of the item inflation and 0.2pp of the coverage. What cannot be fixed by an admission rule is the price: the corpus offers 5,311 asks across 2,453 user turns for 654 required writes - 8.1 asks offered per required write - so a block that reads turns is dominated by asks no write will ever settle (3,069 of its 3,699 items end open, 1,251 of them needed by nobody). The replication repeats it: 156 of 156 recovered, 95.0%, 3,506 items, 16.47 each.

rounds.title: measure the block the product displays, not the block the instrument builds
rounds.why: R231 settled where to read and priced what reading costs, and both answers point at the one thing this lane has never measured: the block is rendered as `items[:8]`, so an ask stated ninth is never shown to the agent no matter how correct the board is. The clause board's 95.4% coverage is therefore a claim about an artefact nobody sees - its 3,699 items are cut to eight lines - and a rule whose coverage is not displayable cannot ship. The round measures the displayed block instead: at the moment of each graded write, is an open item of that write's family among the first eight the product would render?
rounds.bar: registered in prereg/R232-the-first-eight.md before the reading: displayed coverage at least 73.6% on one scope, a hidden share of at most 20% on the scope that passes it, and a display tax of at most 4 writes on the contract
rounds.outcome: REFUTED on B3 alone, and the refusal belongs to the instrument rather than to the rule. On the control grid the clause board shows an open ask of the write's family for 622 of the 654 required writes (95.1%) and hides 14 of the 636 it reaches (2.2%), so B1 and B2 both hold: R231's 95.4% is not coverage of an artefact nobody sees. B3 fails at +47 writes - 463 shown against the request board's 416 covered, within a tolerance of 4 - and the round's own attribution column proves the cap cannot have caused it, because a cut only removes items and the contract's board reaches 463 both with the cut (463) and without it (463). The +47 is a settlement-rule difference and not a display tax: 416 of the 463 are writes the finished contract board also credits, and 47 are graded writes whose obligation was on the block when the agent acted and which the board cannot account for afterwards. What the round corrects is the lane's model of the block's size: at the moment of a call the clause board holds 8.10 items and the contract's 2.41, not 3,699 - the 3,699 is the finished board - so the cap costs the clause rule 2.2% and the contract nothing, and R231's efficiency objection is an objection to an artefact that is never rendered. The 14 hidden writes are an ordering fact rather than a coverage fact: the one inspected by hand sits at line 9 of a 12-item block, behind five asks of one family of which three are settled, so open-before-settled would have lifted it to line 6. The replication agrees on every column (clause 602 of 643 shown, 93.6%; 19 hidden, 3.1%; tax +50) and R233 registers the ordering before its own reading. No default moves: a rendering measurement is not an accuracy measurement, and the clause rule's shipping argument is now price and visibility rather than accuracy, which is the dispatch R234 prices.

rounds.title: order the eight: open before settled
rounds.why: R232 measured the rendered block and found the cut costs 2.2% rather than the fifth its prereg feared, so the display is not the binding constraint. What remains is that the 14 hidden writes were not hidden by the cap but by the order: the block lists asks in the order they were stated, so a settled ask stated early outranks an open one stated late, and the inspected case needs line nine to be seen. The ordering rule is content-free - open items before settled ones, statement order within each group - so it costs nothing to price and cannot smuggle a model into a measurement that has so far had none.
rounds.bar: registered in prereg/R233-the-order.md before the reading: the clause board shows an open ask for at least 634 of 654 required writes (97.0%), the contract's ordered level is at least its own statement-order level, and the clause board's hidden share falls to 1.0% or less
rounds.outcome: REFUTED on B1 by three writes, and the three writes are the finding. `open before settled` lifts the clause board from 622 to 632 of the 654 required writes (96.6% against a bar of 97.0%), removes ten of R232's fourteen hidden writes (14 to 4, hidden share 2.2% to 0.6%), and costs the contract nothing (463 shown against its own 463 statement-order level, B2 holds). B3 holds on the control grid at 0.6% and fails on the replication at 7 of 621 (1.1%), so the round is refused on both grids and on different bars. The mechanism the prereg named in advance is the one that fired: reach is unchanged at 636, so the residue is bounded by the cap and not by the order - every one of the four is a `modify` ask sitting behind 9 to 39 open asks of other families, and the block that holds 39 open items is 41 items long, nine of them `address`. The successor is therefore `one line per family` rather than `MAX_ITEMS`: a grouping removes the duplication that fills the window, where raising the cap would pay for it. What the round establishes independently of its verdict is that the ordering is free and positive - ten writes recovered, no write lost, no new content, no model - which makes it the first change in this lane that a product could adopt on the rendering alone.

rounds.title: one line per family: the block that fills its window with repetition
rounds.why: R233 removed ten of the fourteen hidden writes and left four, and all four are the same shape: a `modify` ask behind nine to thirty-nine **open** asks of other families, in one case nine of them `address`. The cap is binding on openness rather than on settlement, and the material filling it is repetition - one family stated six times because the user restated it. A block that shows one line per family is the same block with the duplicates folded, which is a rendering rule like R233's and costs nothing to price.
rounds.bar: registered in prereg/R234-one-line.md before the reading: the clause board shows an open ask for at least 645 of 654 required writes (98.6%), the contract's grouped level is at least its own statement-order level measured without the fold (463 on the control grid), and at most 3 of the 636 writes the clause board reaches may be hidden (0.5%)
rounds.outcome: TWO OF THREE, AND THE FAILURE IS THE RESULT. `one line per family` shows an open ask for 636 of 654 required writes - every write the board reaches - and hides none, against R233's 632 shown and 4 hidden; it adds no item (8.10 a call, unchanged) and costs the shipped board nothing (463 shown against the 463 its own statement order measured without the fold). B2 and B3 hold; B1 fails by nine writes (636/654 = 97.2% against a bar of 98.6%) for a reason the registration could not have anticipated and should have: B1's 645 was registered ABOVE the 636 the predecessor had already measured as the reachable set, and a rendering rule cannot display a write whose family the moment board never held. The fold's own column is therefore at its ceiling - 636 of 636 reached, 0.0% hidden, replicated at 621 of 621 - and the residual 18 writes (2.75%) are 15 `modify`, 2 `transfer` and 1 `exchange` whose families are simply absent from the block, four of them on a block with no open ask at all and none on a block with more than three open families. So the rendering axis closes here, by a sharper argument than the one registered: no ordering, fold or cap can show an ask the board does not hold, and the material that is left belongs to admission - which is the dispatch R235 prices at ¥34. The three rendering rounds cost ¥0 between them and moved 622 to 636 shown and 14 to 0 hidden.

rounds.title: the clause rule's accuracy dispatch: does 31.8 more points of covered writes buy a task
rounds.instrument: the tau2 retail grid, two arms over 114 tasks at four attempts each; read with eval/tools/resolution.py for its MDE and with eval/tools/read_anchor.py --scope grouped on the dispatched transcripts for its mechanism
rounds.why: Four rounds were read on a board no model was shown. R231 established where the requirement lives (95.4% coverage against the contract's 63.6%), R232 measured the block the product renders, R233 and R234 closed the rendering axis at zero hidden writes - all for ¥0 and none with a token spent. What no round has measured is whether an agent that reads a live ask for 31.8 more points of the graded writes succeeds more often. The grid's own resolution, computed for ¥0, says a pair of 456-episode arms can see 6.72pp and that the domain's floor is 3.21pp at unlimited attempts, so the round is armed at four attempts for ¥36 and cannot resolve anything smaller than the floor at any price on 114 tasks.
rounds.bar: registered in prereg/R235-clause-accuracy.md before any dispatch: B1 the clause arm is not below the contract arm by more than 3.21pp (the domain's floor); B2 a positive delta must reach 6.72pp, the grid's MDE at four attempts, or it is reported UNRESOLVED rather than as a win; B3 on at least 95% of served blocks the clause arm carries an open ask of the family the episode later writes, measured on the dispatched transcripts
